gen-gf-battambang-inter: Battambang brings compressed ascenders and open-jawed curves with real personality, and Inter underneath keeps its big counters and smooth lines out of the way. Paragraphs would flow without a snag.
gen-gf-battambang-mulish: Mulish draws every glyph with one flat line weight and a large x-height, while Battambang's heading squeezes its ascenders and flares its curves open. That gap is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-battambang-poppins: Quirky, compressed, a bit theatrical. Battambang wears its open-jawed curves up top, with Poppins below offering sturdy, rope-loose lowercase where the heading is all flair and the body is all steadiness.
gen-gf-battambang-roboto-slab: Expressive is the first word for Battambang, with its squeezed ascenders and open-jawed curves in the heading. And Roboto Slab gives the lines a structured, middle-heavy texture with open throats, so a long read would feel orderly.
gen-gf-battambang-rubik: Rubik keeps its lowercase big next to the capitals and its round letters open enough to read at small sizes. Battambang then adds the expressive, compressed heading.
gen-gf-bbh-bartle-fs-literata: Letters floating well apart give BBH Bartle a contemporary, clean look in the heading. Literata answers with a bookish serif, its thin and thick strokes shaped by a restrained rhythm and its curves left unclosed.
gen-gf-bbh-bogle-fs-literata: Tight, ribbon-cut letters with keyhole-squeezed curves mark BBH Bogle out as a modern heading. And Literata, a classic serif with a mild stress in its o and e, softens the page below.
gen-gf-bbh-hegarty-fs-literata: Pinched-neck letters, spaced like fence posts. BBH Hegarty keeps its shapes closed, whereas Literata, a text serif, leaves its curves open and gives its g lightly thinned links and sturdy bowls.
gen-gf-beiruti-fs-literata: Dense as canvas thread, Beiruti traces every outline at a fixed nib width with brush-lifted curve ends. Literata, a text serif, offers the opposite, a soft gradient of weight along each rounded stroke.
gen-gf-belanosima-fs-literata: Constant stroke, top to baseline. Belanosima holds one fixed nib width, while Literata, a text serif, thins its rounded tops slightly, and that difference of line is what the pair offers.
